necessaryFacts: The path collaborator is compared case-insensitively with the runtime caller username.
The endpoint rejects only when the caller is not a site admin, is not the target username, and is not a repository admin.
The bounded caller satisfies all three rejecting terms and receives HTTP 403 before target lookup.
Only a surviving branch loads the target permission and returns it.
cases.conditionExplanation: Explain that self-query, repository-admin, or site-admin status independently prevents this guard's rejection, while the all-false combination blocks the read.

publicIntegrationEvidence.observation: A read collaborator queries their own permission and receives HTTP 200 with read access.
A repository admin queries another collaborator's permission and receives HTTP 200.

necessaryFacts: The POST wrapper calls updateIssueAssignees with isAdd=true.
The issue index is resolved before the repository issue-write decision.
The source checks repository permission, not the caller's token scope, and returns HTTP 403 when repository issue-write is absent.
User-name resolution and AddAssignees are after the permission branch and cannot be reached by the bounded caller.
cases.conditionExplanation: Explain that repository issue-write false blocks before user lookup; with repository issue-write true, an existing requested user can reach AddAssignees, while a missing user is rejected before that effect.

publicIntegrationEvidence.observation: A non-writer using an issue-write-scoped token receives HTTP 403 when adding an assignee.
The repository owner reaches the add-assignee effect and receives HTTP 201.

necessaryFacts: The PUT issue-lock route is guarded by reqToken and reqAdmin before LockIssue.
reqAdmin returns HTTP 403 when both repository-admin and site-admin status are false.
Repository issue-write permission and full token scope do not bypass the route-level admin gate.
Only after the route gate does LockIssue check issue-write permission and conditionally call the lock mutation for an unlocked issue.
cases.conditionExplanation: Explain that both admin conditions false blocks regardless of issue-write; either admin condition true passes this route gate, after which issue-write still controls handler reachability to the lock mutation.

publicIntegrationEvidence.observation: The repository owner locks the issue successfully and the persisted lock state becomes true.
Another authenticated user with an all-scope token receives HTTP 403 on the lock request.

limits: These are development migration tasks selected after method freeze, not protected held-out tasks.
The evaluator decides only the declared fixed-context obligations and does not assert whole-repository or deployment coverage.
Integration tests corroborate bounded relations but were not included in model-visible generation sources.
